title: DO_SIGN: fix or remove the 64-byte pre-hash message path
description:
CRYPTO2DEV_IOC_DO_SIGN has a hash_algo field: if non-empty, the provider hashes digest[] before signing. The description says 'the digest[] field holds a raw message and the provider hashes it before signing.'

But digest[] is __u8 digest[CRYPTO2DEV_HASH_MAXLEN] where CRYPTO2DEV_HASH_MAXLEN = 64 bytes.

This means the in-device hash-then-sign path only works for messages of 64 bytes or less. Every real message to be signed is larger than 64 bytes. A developer reading the API will see hash_algo, assume it handles arbitrary messages, pass their 4KB message, get -EINVAL, and not understand why.

The pre-hash path as implemented is essentially useless: a SHA-256 of a 64-byte message could just as easily be computed by the caller. The only justification for in-device hashing would be to keep the message from leaving the FIPS boundary — but at 64 bytes, that message would always fit inline anyway.

Correct usage is: caller hashes the message (in userspace or via a separate SHA OPERATION fd), passes the digest with hash_algo=''.

HUMAN DECISION NEEDED:

(a) Should the pre-hash path be removed from DO_SIGN/DO_VERIFY?
  Option A: Remove. Set hash_algo to reserved/ignored. Callers always pass a pre-computed digest. The struct field stays (ABI) but is documented as unused (must be zero).
  Option B: Remove and explicitly document: 'digest[] contains a pre-computed hash; use a separate OPERATION fd for hashing.'
  Option C: Keep but fix — replace digest[HASH_MAXLEN] with a message pointer approach or increase buffer size. But increasing to, say, 64KB in the ioctl struct is unreasonable; a pointer brings back the __user pointer problem.
  Option D: Keep the pre-hash path but document the 64-byte limit explicitly so callers know it is only for short messages (challenge/response tokens, etc.).

Recommendation: Option B. The two-fd pattern (hash fd + sign ioctl) is clean and already supported. The pre-hash path at 64 bytes adds complexity without real benefit.

(b) If removing: should hash_algo be repurposed as the 'digest algorithm identifier' (i.e., tells the verifier what hash was used to produce the digest, for RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 padding which embeds the hash OID)?
  This is actually a useful field for RSA signing — the padding needs to know the hash algorithm. For ECDSA the hash is implicit. So hash_algo staying in the struct with a changed meaning (algorithm of the pre-computed digest, not a request to hash) would be a useful clarification.

Work items:
- Update crypto2dev_sign_op and crypto2dev_verify_op structs
- Update DO_SIGN/DO_VERIFY handlers in crypto2dev_fd.c
- Update wolfssl and kcapi provider sign/verify implementations
- Update DESIGN.md usage examples
notes: DECISION 2026-04-17: Option A. Remove pre-hash path. hash_algo is repurposed as the digest algorithm identifier — tells the provider (and padding layer) what hash produced digest[]. For RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 this determines the DigestInfo OID. For ECDSA it is informational. digest[] always contains a pre-computed digest; provider never hashes it. Callers needing to hash a message use a SHA OPERATION fd first.
close_reason: Already implemented: provider.h says MUST NOT hash digest; hash_algo is already the digest-algorithm-identifier, not a pre-hash request
